Sometimes known as catching powder or simply "the catch," this silvered powder was devised to slow the pursuit of House Thrune's fiendish servants. The powder is activated by scattering it in an unoccupied adjacent square. If a devil attempts to translocate to a destination within 30 feet of this square, the powder attempts to counteract the spell with a counteract rank of 3 and a counteract modifier of +13. Regardless of the result, the
is consumed, but if it succeeds at the counteract attempt, the affected devil can't use actions with the teleportation trait for 1 minute.

This thick grease can be applied to up to 5 willing creatures to protect them from dangerous energies. This oil is attuned to one of four energy types (acid, cold, electricity, or fire), chosen when created. When applied, it grants resistance 15 to the attuned energy type and reduces the DC for the flat check to end persistent damage of the attuned energy type by 5.

While the elemental once imprisoned in this flask has long departed, some of its energy is still contained within, ready to be released when the flask is broken. You activate a flask of elements by removing a wax seal from the stopper. If you or anyone else hurls the flask (another Interact action), it explodes where it lands. Your toss can place the center of the explosion—a

—anywhere within 60 feet, though at the GM's discretion, you might need to make an attack roll if the throw is unusually challenging. If no one hurls the flask by the start of your next turn, it shatters harmlessly. The effect of the explosion depends on the type of flask.
The flask explodes in a swirl of frigid air, which has the air and cold traits. Creatures within the area take
save. The ground in the area is coated with ice and becomes difficult terrain for 1 hour.
